39|BACKGROUND
40|Androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) has been the backbone of treatment for
41|metastatic prostate cancer since the 1940s. We assessed whether concomitant
42|treatment with ADT plus docetaxel would result in longer overall survival than that
43|with ADT alone.
44|METHODS
45|We assigned men with metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to receive
46|either ADT plus docetaxel (at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of body-surface
47|area every 3 weeks for six cycles) or ADT alone. The primary objective was to test
48|the hypothesis that the median overall survival would be 33.3% longer among
49|patients receiving docetaxel added to ADT early during therapy than among pa-
50|tients receiving ADT alone.
51|RESULTS
52|A total of 790 patients (median age, 63 years) underwent randomization. After a
53|median follow-up of 28.9 months, the median overall survival was 13.6 months
54|longer with ADT plus docetaxel (combination therapy) than with ADT alone (57.6
55|months vs. 44.0 months; hazard ratio for death in the combination group, 0.61;
56|95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). The median time to bio-
57|chemical, symptomatic, or radiographic progression was 20.2 months in the com-
58|bination group, as compared with 11.7 months in the ADT-alone group (hazard
59|ratio, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.72; P<0.001). The rate of a prostate-specific antigen
60|level of less than 0.2 ng per milliliter at 12 months was 27.7% in the combination
61|group versus 16.8% in the ADT-alone group (P<0.001). In the combination group,
62|the rate of grade 3 or 4 febrile neutropenia was 6.2%, the rate of grade 3 or 4
63|infection with neutropenia was 2.3%, and the rate of grade 3 sensory neuropathy
64|and of grade 3 motor neuropathy was 0.5%.
65|CONCLUSIONS
66|Six cycles of docetaxel at the beginning of ADT for metastatic prostate cancer re-
67|sulted in significantly longer overall survival than that with ADT alone. (Funded by
68|the National Cancer Institute and others; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00309985.)

5|egressions of metastatic prostate
6|cancer were first documented in the 1940s
7|and were achieved with surgical castra-
8|tion; subsequently, androgen-deprivation therapy
9|(ADT) became the mainstay of therapy.1 Attempts
10|to improve the efficacy or decrease the treatment
11|burden of ADT have included the use of anti
12|androgens alone, intermittent dosing of ADT,
13|and the use of an antiandrogen combined with
14|medical or surgical castration.2-4 A meta-analysis
15|revealed an increase in survival of 3 percentage
16|points at 5 years with concurrent use of a non-
17|steroidal antiandrogen at the time of initiation
18|of ADT.2 However, resistance to ADT occurs in
19|most patients, with the result that the median
20|survival among patients with metastatic prostate
21|cancer is approximately 3 years.5,6 In patients
22|with resistance to ADT, docetaxel therapy re-
23|sulted in a median survival that was approxi-
24|mately 2.5 months longer than that with mito-
25|xantrone and prednisone.7,8
26|Prior studies of chemotherapy plus ADT, which
27|did not show a benefit, were small studies that
28|involved primarily patients with a relatively low
29|tumor burden.9,10 Definitions of a high burden of
30|disease have included the presence of visceral
31|metastases, a bone-metastasis burden categorized
32|by site (beyond the axial skeleton) or by a high
33|number of lesions, or a combination of these.9,11,12
34|In this study, the E3805 study, patients received
35|ADT alone or ADT plus docetaxel at the begin-
36|ning of ADT for metastatic hormone-sensitive
37|prostate cancer, and stratification was performed
38|prospectively according to high or low burden of
39|metastatic disease.
40|Methods
41|Study Oversight
42|The primary objective of the E3805 study was to
43|determine whether docetaxel therapy at the be-
44|ginning of ADT for metastatic hormone-sensitive
45|prostate cancer would result in longer overall
46|survival than that with ADT alone. The study was
47|designed in 2005 by the Eastern Cooperative On-
48|cology Group (ECOG; now part of ECOG-ACRIN)
49|and was approved by the institutional review
50|board at each participating institution. The study
51|was coordinated by the ECOG-ACRIN Cancer
52|Research Group. The ECOG-ACRIN Statistical
53|Center collected the data and was the leading
54|cooperative group and data coordinating center.
55|The first two authors attest that the study was
56|conducted and monitored as specified by the
57|protocol. The first author wrote the first draft of
58|the manuscript, with subsequent contributions
59|by all the coauthors. The authors vouch for the
60|accuracy and completeness of the data presented.
61|The protocol with the statistical analysis plan
62|is available with the full text of this article at
63|NEJM.org. Sanofi donated the docetaxel for
64|early use (i.e., before progression during ADT)
65|and provided a grant to ECOG-ACRIN but had
66|no role in the design of the protocol, the collec-
67|tion or analysis of the data, or the preparation of
68|the manuscript.
69|Patients
70|Patients were enrolled by ECOG-ACRIN, the
71|Southwest Oncology Group, the Alliance for
72|Clinical Trials in Oncology, and NRG Oncology
73|(a merged group that includes the National Sur-
74|gical Adjuvant Breast and Bowel Project, the Ra-
75|diation Therapy Oncology Group, and the Gyne-
76|cologic Oncology Group) and through the Clinical
77|Trials Support Unit. Eligible patients had a
78|pathological diagnosis of prostate cancer or a
79|clinical scenario consistent with prostate cancer
80|with an elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA)
81|level; radiologic evidence of metastatic disease;
82|and an ECOG performance-status score of 0, 1,
83|or 2 (on a scale from 0 to 5, with higher scores
84|indicating greater disability; patients with a score
85|of 2 were eligible if the decrement in function-
86|ing was due to prostate cancer). Prior adjuvant
87|ADT was allowed if the duration of therapy was
88|24 months or less and progression had occurred
89|more than 12 months after completion of ther-
90|apy. Patients who were receiving ADT for meta-
91|static disease were eligible if there was no evidence
92|of progression and treatment had commenced
93|within 120 days before randomization. Organ
94|function that was adequate for docetaxel treat-
95|ment was required (details are provided in the
96|protocol). All patients provided written informed
97|consent in accordance with institutional and
98|federal guidelines.
99|Treatment Plan, Stratification,
100|and Randomization
101|Patients were randomly assigned to ADT alone
102|or to combination therapy with ADT plus doce
103|taxel at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of
104|body-surface area given every 3 weeks for six

4|cycles, with premedication with 8 mg of oral
5|dexamethasone at 12 hours, 3 hours, and 1 hour
6|before docetaxel infusion. Daily prednisone was
7|not required. Patients were stratified according
8|to age (<70 years vs. ≥70 years), ECOG perfor-
9|mance-status score (0 or 1 vs. 2), and planned
10|use of combined androgen blockade for more
11|than 30 days (yes vs. no) or agents approved for
12|prevention of skeletal-related events in castration-
13|resistant disease (zoledronic acid or denosumab)
14|(yes vs. no). Patients were also stratified accord-
15|ing to the duration of prior adjuvant ADT (<12
16|months vs. ≥12 months) and the extent of metas-
17|tases (high volume [defined as the presence of
18|visceral metastases or ≥4 bone lesions with ≥1
19|beyond the vertebral bodies and pelvis] vs. low
20|volume). Patients were required to take at least
21|500 mg of oral calcium carbonate and at least
22|400 IU of vitamin D per day.
23|Dose Modifications
24|No dose modifications of ADT were allowed,
25|and the use of a nonsteroidal antiandrogen with
26|castration (medical or surgical) at the time of
27|initiation of therapy was at the discretion of the
28|investigator. Intermittent hormonal therapy was
29|not allowed. For docetaxel, no more than two
30|dose modifications (decreases to 65 mg per
31|square meter and 55 mg per square meter) were
32|allowed. Dose adjustments were made according
33|to the organ system that showed the greatest de-
34|gree of toxic effects, which were graded accord-
35|ing to the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Com-
36|mon Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events
37|(CTCAE; version 3.0 until September 2011 and
38|version 4.0 thereafter). Details on dosing are
39|provided in the protocol. If a dose was reduced
40|owing to toxic effects, it was not increased sub-
41|sequently, and docetaxel was discontinued if
42|administration was delayed longer than 3 weeks
43|from the scheduled day of dosing. The use of
44|growth factors was at the discretion of the inves-
45|tigator.
46|Monitoring of Toxic Effects and Efficacy
47|Patients assigned to combination therapy were
48|seen every 3 weeks during the period of docetaxel
49|administration and then every 3 months. Patients
50|assigned to ADT alone were seen every 3 months.
51|For the reporting of serious adverse events to the
52|NCI and to guide dose modifications, CTCAE
53|version 3.0 was used until September 2011, at
54|which time the study began using version 4.0. To
55|ensure consistency, case-report forms for toxic
56|effects that were recorded in the study database
57|retained the use of version 3.0. All grade 3 or
58|higher toxic effects in the combination group
59|were captured, and an attribution of relatedness
60|to study therapy was made by the local investiga-
61|tors. Adverse events among patients assigned to
62|ADT alone were not routinely documented, al-
63|though major adverse events were to be reported.
64|PSA levels were measured at each scheduled
65|visit. Imaging (computed tomography [CT] of
66|the abdomen and pelvis, technetium-99m bone
67|scanning, and radiography or CT of the chest)
68|was performed at baseline and at the time of
69|documented castration resistance or as clinically
70|indicated. Disease progression on imaging was
71|determined according to the Response Evaluation
72|Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST), version 1.013
73|(the criteria are summarized in the protocol). A
74|complete serologic response was defined as a
75|PSA level of less than 0.2 ng per milliliter on two
76|consecutive measurements at least 4 weeks apart.
77|Serologic progression was defined as an increase
78|in the PSA level of more than 50% above the
79|nadir reached after the initiation of ADT, with
80|two consecutive increases at least 2 weeks apart.
81|The date of a first recorded increase of more
82|than 50% above the nadir was deemed the date
83|of progression. If the nadir level was less than
84|2 ng per milliliter, a minimum increase of more
85|than 2 ng per milliliter was required.
86|All time-to-event end points were determined
87|from the time of randomization. Overall survival
88|was defined as the time until death from any
89|cause. The time to castration-resistant prostate
90|cancer was defined as the time until document-
91|ed clinical or serologic progression with a testos-
92|terone level of less than 50 ng per deciliter (or
93|source documentation of medical castration or
94|surgical castration). The time to clinical pro-
95|gression was defined as the time until increas-
96|ing symptoms of bone metastases; progression
97|according to RECIST, version 1.0; or clinical
98|deterioration due to cancer according to the in-
99|vestigator's opinion.
100|Statistical Analysis
101|The study underwent two major amendments
102|(details are provided in the protocol); in all ver-
103|sions, an intention-to-treat analysis plan was
104|used. With each amendment, the sample size

4|was adjusted so that the study would have 80%
5|power to detect a 33.3% difference in median
6|overall survival between the combination group
7|and the ADT-alone group, with the use of a
8|stratified log-rank test at a one-sided alpha level
9|of 2.5%. At study inception, only patients with
10|high-volume disease were to be enrolled, and the
11|sample size was to be 568 patients. After com-
12|pletion of enrollment in the NCI-sponsored
13|S9346 trial,4 an amendment to the E3805 study
14|was made in July 2008, after 53 patients had been
15|enrolled, to include patients with low-volume
16|disease. A prospective stratification of high vol-
17|ume versus low volume of metastatic disease
18|was added, and the sample size was increased to
19|600 patients. The final amendment was made in
20|December 2011, after 579 patients had been en-
21|rolled, to reflect new data documenting an in-
22|crease in median overall survival owing to the
23|use of PSA in the detection and monitoring of
24|disease activity5 (initial projections were based
25|on studies from the pre-PSA era) and to address
26|the September 2011 report of the data and safety
27|monitoring committee, which noted that 70% of
28|enrolled patients had high-volume disease. The
29|final design required the enrollment of 780 pa-
30|tients, with projections of median overall sur-
31|vival with ADT alone of 33 months among pa-
32|tients with high-volume disease and 67 months
33|among patients with low-volume disease.
34|Interim analyses were to be performed before
35|all semiannual meetings of the data and safety
36|monitoring committee starting when approxi-
37|mately 25% of the planned full information was
38|obtained and continuing until either the criteria
39|for early stopping were met or full information
40|was obtained (after 399 deaths). The study was
41|monitored for early stopping for futility with the
42|use of repeated-confidence-interval methods.14 At
43|each interim analysis, the nominal (1 - [2 × alpha])
44|confidence interval for the hazard ratio for death
45|in the comparison of the combination-therapy
46|group with the ADT-alone group was computed.
47|For a given analysis time (information fraction),
48|alpha was set at the nominal one-sided signifi-
49|cance level of the use function boundary. Infor-
50|mation from interim analyses was reviewed by
51|members of the independent data and safety
52|monitoring committee, who determined wheth-
53|er efficacy or futility had been demonstrated and
54|who decided whether the study should be stopped
55|and the results reported early.
56|Descriptive statistics were used to characterize
57|patients at study entry. Kaplan-Meier estimates15
58|were used for event-time distributions. Cox pro-
59|portional-hazard models,16 stratified according
60|to the factors described above, were used to esti-
61|mate hazard ratios for time-to-event end points.
62|Stratified log-rank tests17 were used to compare
63|event-time distributions between the two groups.
64|Response rates were compared with the use of
65|Fisher's exact test.18 An intention-to-treat analy-
66|sis was conducted that included all randomly
67|assigned patients regardless of eligibility and
68|treatment status. P values are two-sided, and con-
69|fidence intervals are at the 95% level.
70|Results
71|Patients
72|From July 2006 through December 2012, a total
73|of 790 patients were enrolled and underwent ran-
74|domization. Ten patients were ineligible, 7 had
75|incomplete information to assess eligibility, and
76|6 patients in the combination group did not
77|start the assigned therapy (Fig. S1 in the Supple-
78|mentary Appendix, available at NEJM.org). All
79|randomly assigned patients were followed and
80|included in the primary analysis of their assigned
81|group. At the planned interim analysis in Octo-
82|ber 2013, a total of 53% of the planned full in-
83|formation had been obtained, prespecified crite-
84|ria for significance had been met, and the data
85|were released by the data and safety monitoring
86|committee. This report represents data with a
87|cutoff date for survival of December 23, 2013;
88|the median follow-up was 28.9 months, with
89|136 deaths in the ADT-alone group and 101
90|deaths in the combination group. All other data
91|reflect the database as of December 23, 2014.
92|Patient characteristics were well balanced be-
93|tween the two groups (Table 1). The median age
94|was 64 years (range, 36 to 88) in the combina-
95|tion group and 63 years (range, 39 to 91) in the

101|higher (on a scale from 2 to 10, with higher
102|scores indicating a more aggressive form of pros-
103|tate cancer and a worse prognosis). In both
104|groups, 73% of the patients had received no

4|docetaxel given at the time ADT was initiated for
5|hormone-sensitive disease resulted in better can-
6|cer control than that with ADT alone, with a
7|longer time to the development of castration resis-
8|tance, a higher rate of decrease of the PSA level
9|to less than 0.2 ng per milliliter at 12 months, a
10|lower number of prostate-cancer deaths, and
11|substantially longer overall survival. The longer
12|overall survival than that with ADT alone was
13|achieved despite the fact that almost half the 287
14|patients who received ADT alone and then met
15|the criteria for castration resistance received
16|docetaxel at the time of disease progression
17|along with other therapies that prolong overall
18|survival in patients with metastatic castration-
19|resistant prostate cancer.
20|The definition of high-volume disease used
21|for this protocol was a combination of features
22|from prior classifications. All the definitions
23|included the presence of nonnodal, soft-tissue
24|visceral disease as a predictor of poor prognosis.
25|This protocol made use of sites of bone metas-
26|tases and the number of metastases to avoid
27|classifying patients with three or fewer sites as
28|having high-volume disease even if one lesion
29|was beyond the vertebrae and pelvis (any lesion
30|beyond the vertebrae and pelvis, irrespective of
31|total lesion count, would be classified as "exten-
32|sive" according to the definition of the South-
33|west Oncology Group4). In the subgroup of pa-
34|tients with high-volume disease, the median
35|overall survival was 17.0 months longer in the
36|combination group than in the ADT-alone group
37|(49.2 months vs. 32.2 months). On the basis of
38|an unpublished analysis of data from the S9346
39|trial5 we had projected a median survival of
40|33 months among patients with high-volume
41|disease (according to the definition used in our
42|protocol) in the ADT-alone group, and as such,
43|the definition was reproducible across two phase
44|3 studies conducted in a similar time period.
45|A previously reported randomized study in-
46|volving 380 patients (the GETUG-AFU 15 study),
47|which had a similar design to that of the current
48|study, did not detect longer overall survival with

53|- and was first analyzed in 2011, before there

questions.wording: Was the allocation sequence random?
questions.official_guidance: Answer ‘Yes’ if a random component was used in the sequence generation process. Examples include computer-generated random numbers; reference to a random number table; coin tossing; shuffling cards or envelopes; throwing dice; or drawing lots. Answer ‘No’ if no random element was used in generating the allocation sequence or the sequence is predictable. Answer ‘No information’ if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 17, Box 4, signalling question 1.1
questions.bias_construct: Whether a random component was used to generate the allocation sequence.
questions.decision_rule: Answer yes when a random component was used; answer no when no random element was used or the sequence is predictable. A statement that the study is randomized alone supports no_information.
evidence_needed: The sequence-generation method, such as computer random numbers, a random number table, coin tossing, or minimization with a random element.
questions.no_information_rule: Answer no_information when the only information about randomization methods is that the study is randomized. Do not turn missing reporting into proof that the sequence was non-random.

considerations: Minimization should generally be considered random when it includes a random element.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.

As an additional secondary endpoint, Quality of Life, including benefit and

6.5.1
Overall Quality of Life
The Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Prostate (FACT- P) is
a self-report measure of both general and disease-specific quality of
life (40). The FACT-P (version 4) contains 39 likert items distributed
over 5 subscales: Physical (7 items), Social (7 items), Emotional (6
items), and Functional (7 items) well-being, and the additional
concerns related to Prostate Cancer Scale (12 items). The FACT-P is
scored by summing responses to the items in each subscale. The
subscale scores are then combined to create a total QOL score. A
trial outcome index (TOI) can also be calculated by summing the
Physical and Functional Well-being Scales and the Prostate Cancer
Scale. The FACT-P requires only a sixth-grade reading level and can
be completed in 8 - 10 minutes (41).

BACKGROUND
Androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) has been the backbone of treatment for
metastatic prostate cancer since the 1940s. We assessed whether concomitant
treatment with ADT plus docetaxel would result in longer overall survival than that
with ADT alone.
METHODS
We assigned men with metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to receive
either ADT plus docetaxel (at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of body-surface
area every 3 weeks for six cycles) or ADT alone. The primary objective was to test
the hypothesis that the median overall survival would be 33.3% longer among
patients receiving docetaxel added to ADT early during therapy than among pa-
tients receiving ADT alone.
RESULTS
A total of 790 patients (median age, 63 years) underwent randomization. After a
median follow-up of 28.9 months, the median overall survival was 13.6 months
longer with ADT plus docetaxel (combination therapy) than with ADT alone (57.6
months vs. 44.0 months; hazard ratio for death in the combination group, 0.61;
95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). The median time to bio-
chemical, symptomatic, or radiographic progression was 20.2 months in the com-
bination group, as compared with 11.7 months in the ADT-alone group (hazard
ratio, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.72; P<0.001). The rate of a prostate-specific antigen
level of less than 0.2 ng per milliliter at 12 months was 27.7% in the combination
group versus 16.8% in the ADT-alone group (P<0.001). In the combination group,
the rate of grade 3 or 4 febrile neutropenia was 6.2%, the rate of grade 3 or 4
infection with neutropenia was 2.3%, and the rate of grade 3 sensory neuropathy
and of grade 3 motor neuropathy was 0.5%.
CONCLUSIONS
Six cycles of docetaxel at the beginning of ADT for metastatic prostate cancer re-
sulted in significantly longer overall survival than that with ADT alone. (Funded by
the National Cancer Institute and others; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00309985.)

I’m grounding each of those judgments in the cited passages now.

# Assess randomization

Use this reference for Domain 1. The returned question cards supply the exact
wording, allowed answer values, guidance, and activation rules.

Keep three propositions separate:

1. **Sequence generation:** Was the allocation sequence random?
2. **Allocation concealment:** Was allocation concealed until participants were
   enrolled and assigned?
3. **Baseline differences:** Do observed imbalances suggest a problem with the
   randomization process rather than chance?

Sequence methods such as computer generation, random-number tables, lots, or
minimization may support the first proposition. Identify the random component;
concealing a predictable formula does not make it random.
For concealment, assess the pre-assignment mechanism and who could access the next
assignment. When reported facts support a probable judgment, state the inferred
safeguard or weakness. Preserve `no_information` when the details and trial
circumstances do not support that judgment.

For baseline differences, inspect the complete arm-specific baseline table or
list and any explanation. Different values are not automatically evidence of a
randomization problem. Missing reporting is not evidence that randomization
failed.

Select complete premises. A Methods heading, the word "randomized," or a
list-introducing sentence alone does not answer these questions.

When a randomization premise remains unresolved, use the active Source
inventory to include appendices, supplements, or combined documents that may
describe the actual sequence or concealment procedure. Search with concrete
study wording from the report. Continue a cursor, issue another bounded query,
or widen the Source scope when it could resolve the premise. Read the full
procedure before selecting Evidence. Stop when the complete premise is
supported or record the bounded information limit. Source role, an unopened
document, and a no-hit query do not establish how allocation was performed.

questions.wording: Was the allocation sequence random?
questions.official_guidance: Answer ‘Yes’ if a random component was used in the sequence generation process. Examples include computer-generated random numbers; reference to a random number table; coin tossing; shuffling cards or envelopes; throwing dice; or drawing lots. Answer ‘No’ if no random element was used in generating the allocation sequence or the sequence is predictable. Answer ‘No information’ if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 17, Box 4, signalling question 1.1
questions.bias_construct: Whether a random component was used to generate the allocation sequence.
questions.decision_rule: Answer yes when a random component was used; answer no when no random element was used or the sequence is predictable. A statement that the study is randomized alone supports no_information.
evidence_needed: The sequence-generation method, such as computer random numbers, a random number table, coin tossing, or minimization with a random element.
questions.no_information_rule: Answer no_information when the only information about randomization methods is that the study is randomized. Do not turn missing reporting into proof that the sequence was non-random.

answer_anchors.text: A random component was used in sequence generation.
No random element was used, or the sequence was predictable.

considerations: Minimization should generally be considered random when it includes a random element.

Sequence generation asks how the allocation sequence was produced; concealment asks whether forthcoming assignments were hidden before enrolment and assignment; baseline imbalance asks whether the resulting groups suggest a randomization problem. Evidence for one does not answer the others.

guidance: Answer every initially active question plus each dependent question whose activation predicate is met by your earlier answers. Extra inactive branch answers are ignored and never committed. Preserve the approved Result target.

Review the inspected passages against its exact proposition and check material contradictions. Reuse adequate Evidence. Inspect returned passages before using them. A limitation requires that explicit premise and stopping rationale; include a Trial-scoped search receipt when retrieval provenance is useful, but a direct read does not require a search receipt. Absence requires a scoped untruncated no-hit receipt.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.
response_framework.quotation_rule: Brief direct quotations from the text of the study report should be used whenever possible to support the answer.

traps: A no-hit search describes one lexical query, not scientific absence.

Different treatment or visit schedules do not by themselves prove that outcome measurement differed between groups.
Stratification does not prove allocation concealment.

clinical progression. Clinical progression is defined as increasing
symptomatic bone metastases, progression per RECIST criteria or
clinical deterioration due to cancer per investigator's opinion.
6.4.4
Time to Serological Progression Free Survival:
The interval between randomization and the date of documented PSA
progression. Progression will be declared if patient has documented
to have a testosterone less than 50 ng/dL. In cases where a
testosterone level has not been obtained and patient has not had an
orchiectomy (as detailed in the study calendar), PD will be deemed if
patient had a documented rise in PSA on LHRH analogue therapy.
6.5
Quality of Life (FACT-P)
As an additional secondary endpoint, Quality of Life, including benefit and
adverse effects of the treatment and the disease, will be measured in all patients.
6.5.1
Overall Quality of Life
The Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Prostate (FACT- P) is
a self-report measure of both general and disease-specific quality of
life (40). The FACT-P (version 4) contains 39 likert items distributed
over 5 subscales: Physical (7 items), Social (7 items), Emotional (6
items), and Functional (7 items) well-being, and the additional
concerns related to Prostate Cancer Scale (12 items). The FACT-P is
scored by summing responses to the items in each subscale. The
subscale scores are then combined to create a total QOL score. A
trial outcome index (TOI) can also be calculated by summing the
Physical and Functional Well-being Scales and the Prostate Cancer
Scale. The FACT-P requires only a sixth-grade reading level and can
be completed in 8 - 10 minutes (41).
The FACT-P scales have been widely used to evaluate quality of life
in clinical trials for prostate cancer treatments. Internal consistency of
the FACT-P (version 4) subscales ranges from .85 to .89. Concurrent,
construct and discriminant validity has been documented (41).
Sensitivity to change in performance status and PSA score over two
months has been demonstrated for the Physical Well-being,
Functional Well-being, Prostate Cancer Scales, the Trial Outcome
Index, and the total FACT-P (version 4) scale (41).
The FACT-P instrument has been validated in samples of patients
with extensive disease prostate cancer (41), and used to assess

(the criteria are summarized in the protocol). A

Serologic progression was defined as an increase
in the PSA level of more than 50% above the
nadir reached after the initiation of ADT, with
two consecutive increases at least 2 weeks apart.
The date of a first recorded increase of more

of progression. If the nadir level was less than
2 ng per milliliter, a minimum increase of more
than 2 ng per milliliter was required.
All time-to-event end points were determined
from the time of randomization. Overall survival
was defined as the time until death from any
cause. The time to castration-resistant prostate
cancer was defined as the time until document-
ed clinical or serologic progression with a testos-
terone level of less than 50 ng per deciliter (or
source documentation of medical castration or
surgical castration). The time to clinical pro-
gression was defined as the time until increas-
ing symptoms of bone metastases; progression
according to RECIST, version 1.0; or clinical
deterioration due to cancer according to the in-

guidance: Answer every initially active question plus each dependent question whose activation predicate is met by your earlier answers. Extra inactive branch answers are ignored and never committed. Preserve the approved Result target.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.
response_framework.quotation_rule: Brief direct quotations from the text of the study report should be used whenever possible to support the answer.

traps: A no-hit search describes one lexical query, not scientific absence.
A planned method does not prove conduct; a time origin or analysis population does not prove complete follow-up or equal assessment.
An endpoint label or definition does not prove objectivity, blinding, prespecification, or no alternative analyses.
A treatment assignment or visibly different intervention does not by itself prove that participants or personnel knew the assignment.
Different treatment or visit schedules do not by themselves prove that outcome measurement differed between groups.
Stratification does not prove allocation concealment.

Endpoint Definitions
6.4.1
Overall Survival
Survival will be measured as the period from randomization until
death due to any cause.
6.4.2
Time to Hormone Refractory Disease:
The interval between randomization and the date of documented
clinical or serological progression with testosterone less than 50
ng/dL.
6.4.3
Time to Clinical Progression Free Survival:
The interval between randomization and the date of documented
clinical progression. Clinical progression is defined as increasing
symptomatic bone metastases, progression per RECIST criteria or
clinical deterioration due to cancer per investigator's opinion.
6.4.4
Time to Serological Progression Free Survival:
The interval between randomization and the date of documented PSA
progression. Progression will be declared if patient has documented
to have a testosterone less than 50 ng/dL. In cases where a
testosterone level has not been obtained and patient has not had an
orchiectomy (as detailed in the study calendar), PD will be deemed if
patient had a documented rise in PSA on LHRH analogue therapy.
6.5
Quality of Life (FACT-P)
As an additional secondary endpoint, Quality of Life, including benefit and
adverse effects of the treatment and the disease, will be measured in all patients.
6.5.1
Overall Quality of Life
The Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Prostate (FACT- P) is
a self-report measure of both general and disease-specific quality of
life (40). The FACT-P (version 4) contains 39 likert items distributed
over 5 subscales: Physical (7 items), Social (7 items), Emotional (6
items), and Functional (7 items) well-being, and the additional
concerns related to Prostate Cancer Scale (12 items). The FACT-P is
scored by summing responses to the items in each subscale. The
subscale scores are then combined to create a total QOL score. A
trial outcome index (TOI) can also be calculated by summing the
Physical and Functional Well-being Scales and the Prostate Cancer
Scale. The FACT-P requires only a sixth-grade reading level and can
be completed in 8 - 10 minutes (41).
The FACT-P scales have been widely used to evaluate quality of life
in clinical trials for prostate cancer treatments. Internal consistency of
the FACT-P (version 4) subscales ranges from .85 to .89. Concurrent,
construct and discriminant validity has been documented (41).
Sensitivity to change in performance status and PSA score over two
months has been demonstrated for the Physical Well-being,
Functional Well-being, Prostate Cancer Scales, the Trial Outcome
Index, and the total FACT-P (version 4) scale (41).

with extensive disease prostate cancer (41), and used to assess

Monitoring of Toxic Effects and Efficacy
Patients assigned to combination therapy were
seen every 3 weeks during the period of docetaxel
administration and then every 3 months. Patients
assigned to ADT alone were seen every 3 months.
For the reporting of serious adverse events to the
NCI and to guide dose modifications, CTCAE
version 3.0 was used until September 2011, at
which time the study began using version 4.0. To
ensure consistency, case-report forms for toxic
effects that were recorded in the study database
retained the use of version 3.0. All grade 3 or
higher toxic effects in the combination group
were captured, and an attribution of relatedness
to study therapy was made by the local investiga-
tors. Adverse events among patients assigned to
ADT alone were not routinely documented, al-
though major adverse events were to be reported.

documents the use of other therapies that have

evidence.quote:
We assigned men with metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to receive
either ADT plus docetaxel (at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of body-surface
area every 3 weeks for six cycles) or ADT alone. The primary objective was to test
the hypothesis that the median overall survival would be 33.3% longer among
patients receiving docetaxel added to ADT early during therapy than among pa-
tients receiving ADT alone.

answers.justification: The groups received visibly different regimens: ADT plus six docetaxel cycles versus ADT alone, and the combination group attended every three weeks during docetaxel while the ADT-alone group attended every three months. Participants were therefore likely aware of assignment.

Clinicians administering docetaxel and managing its toxicities would know which participants received the chemotherapy regimen. The report describes different visit schedules and local investigators attributing serious toxicities to study therapy, making personnel awareness highly likely.

The protocol permitted dose reductions and delays for toxicity, so these planned treatment changes are not protocol-inconsistent deviations. The report says six patients assigned to docetaxel did not start and some who started did not complete all cycles, but it does not link these cases to trial-context pressure or other context-caused departures. Subsequent docetaxel and other therapies in the ADT-alone group were given after castration-resistant disease developed; that is subsequent treatment after progression, not evidence that trial context caused deviations affecting this endpoint.
unknowns: The reasons why six patients assigned to docetaxel did not start treatment and why some treated patients did not complete all planned cycles.

counterevidence.implication: The report documents that six participants did not start assigned therapy and that not all who started completed all cycles; reasons are not provided, so these are potential departures but do not establish that the trial context caused them.

answers.justification: The report states that the intention-to-treat analysis included all randomized participants regardless of eligibility and treatment status, and that all randomized participants were followed and included in the analysis of their assigned group. The clinical-progression result is presented for the full randomized arm denominators, 397 and 393, consistent with estimating the effect of assignment.

questions.wording: Were data for this outcome available for all, or nearly all, participants randomized?
questions.official_guidance: ‘Nearly all’ should be interpreted as that the number of participants with missing outcome data is sufficiently small that their outcomes, whatever they were, could have made no important difference to the estimated effect of intervention. For continuous outcomes, availability of data from 95% of the participants will often be sufficient. Note that imputed data should be regarded as missing data.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 45, Box 8, signalling question 3.1
questions.bias_construct: Whether outcome data were available for all or nearly all randomized participants.
questions.decision_rule: Use the randomized population. Yes or probably yes requires evidence that outcome data were available for all or nearly all participants. No or probably no requires evidence of materially incomplete availability. When the extent remains unknown, use no_information. Judge whether the missing outcomes, whatever they were, could make an important difference to this Result; no universal percentage threshold applies. Imputed data count as missing.
evidence_needed: For yes or probably yes, actual outcome-availability evidence can be comparable observed-outcome counts, arm-specific loss-to-follow-up or censoring accounting, or an explicit complete/nearly-complete ascertainment statement.

Compare the approved outcome/time point across participant-flow and outcome-data passages. For each comparable arm or unit distinguish the randomized denominator, outcome-observed count, analysed count, imputed count, post-randomization excluded count, and event count. An event count is a numerator, not an outcome-observed count; an analysis denominator is not necessarily an outcome-observed count. Calculate randomized minus observed only when population, arm, unit, and time point are the same. Imputed data count as missing.

Keep outcome availability separate from mitigation quality: a sensitivity analysis or imputation does not change the observed count, and observed cannot be inferred as analysed minus imputed unless the source establishes the same population, time window, and mutually exclusive counts.
questions.no_information_rule: Answer no_information when the extent of missing outcome data remains unknown after bounded retrieval. Lack of evidence for complete availability is not evidence of materially incomplete availability.

answer_anchors.text: Outcome data were available for all or nearly all randomized participants.
Outcome data were not available for all or nearly all randomized participants.
The report provides no information about the extent of missing outcome data.

considerations: The appropriate population is all randomized participants, not only participants included in a final analysis. Keep outcome availability distinct from exclusions for analysis or conduct; the same passage may inform both Domains for different scientific reasons.

Distinguish administrative censoring at a common data cutoff from censoring caused by missing follow-up; inspect actual rates and follow-up accounting rather than treating a generic censoring rule as outcome-availability evidence.

For time-to-event Results, treatment discontinuation or last-known-alive censoring does not by itself establish that outcome observation stopped; identify the actual observation endpoint, censoring reason, and follow-up pathway. For mortality, recovery or discharge does not establish vital status at a later time point. A total combining completed follow-up, recovery, and death does not establish mortality availability. If availability remains unresolved, inspect outcome-status or missing-value tables, including supplements. Match their outcome and time window to the approved Result. For dichotomous outcomes, compare unknown outcomes with observed events. Recovery may inform bias from missingness, but does not make unknown vital status observed.

Neutral paired control: complete ascertainment and an analysis denominator with unresolved ascertainment differ only in the availability premise; administrative censoring and worsening-related follow-up loss differ only in the missingness mechanism.

guidance: Answer every initially active question plus each dependent question whose activation predicate is met by your earlier answers. Extra inactive branch answers are ignored and never committed. Preserve the approved Result target.

Evaluate activated questions in question order. Submit every activated question with a justification, unknowns, and counterevidence. Review the inspected passages against its exact proposition and check material contradictions. Reuse adequate Evidence. When a premise remains unresolved, state the unresolved premise and why you stopped, and use bounded discovery across relevant Sources, including a protocol or SAP when relevant. Inspect returned passages before using them. A limitation requires that explicit premise and stopping rationale; include a Trial-scoped search receipt when retrieval provenance is useful, but a direct read does not require a search receipt. Absence requires a scoped untruncated no-hit receipt.

Cite complete premises for the active question. One passage may support several facts. When an answer depends on separate passages, cite each with its own boundaries. A relationship kind describes the use of Evidence; it adds no scientific fact.

When inference, conflict, or uncertainty connects Evidence to an answer, include a concise question-specific justification. State what the passages establish, what remains unresolved, and why the selected option follows. Any support relationship is host-asserted: the server checks structure, ownership, and exact Evidence provenance but does not independently judge semantic entailment.

Working premise records are source-grounded resumable notes. Reuse them only when the working checkpoint is current for this exact approved Result and captured Source projection; a stale checkpoint requires the stated recovery action and never carries a prior Domain judgment into this assessment.
A definitive yes or no needs direct_support, indirect_support, or contradiction; a limitation or absence alone supports uncertainty, not a definitive answer.

Evaluate activation against your draft answers. If validation reports missing active question IDs, add those questions with allowed answer values and supported bases, then resubmit the complete active set in one validation call. The server commits only active answers.

Apply every reported repair and retain other drafted answers. Add missing questions to the existing answer set. Resolve further activation from the repaired answers before resubmitting. The server ignores inactive answers.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.
response_framework.quotation_rule: Brief direct quotations from the text of the study report should be used whenever possible to support the answer.

traps: A no-hit search describes one lexical query, not scientific absence.
A planned method does not prove conduct; a time origin or analysis population does not prove complete follow-up or equal assessment.
An endpoint label or definition does not prove objectivity, blinding, prespecification, or no alternative analyses.
A treatment assignment or visibly different intervention does not by itself prove that participants or personnel knew the assignment.
Different treatment or visit schedules do not by themselves prove that outcome measurement differed between groups.
Stratification does not prove allocation concealment.
data.completion_rule: Ground each active proposition and its uncertainty in inspected Evidence or bounded discovery for unresolved premises. Supply every question activated by the submitted answer path with an Evidence use, scoped absence receipt, or limitation. Inactive extras are ignored.

We assigned men with metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to receive
either ADT plus docetaxel (at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of body-surface

questions.wording: Were data for this outcome available for all, or nearly all, participants randomized?
questions.official_guidance: ‘Nearly all’ should be interpreted as that the number of participants with missing outcome data is sufficiently small that their outcomes, whatever they were, could have made no important difference to the estimated effect of intervention. For continuous outcomes, availability of data from 95% of the participants will often be sufficient. Note that imputed data should be regarded as missing data.

questions.bias_construct: Whether outcome data were available for all or nearly all randomized participants.
questions.decision_rule: Use the randomized population. Yes or probably yes requires evidence that outcome data were available for all or nearly all participants. No or probably no requires evidence of materially incomplete availability. When the extent remains unknown, use no_information. Judge whether the missing outcomes, whatever they were, could make an important difference to this Result; no universal percentage threshold applies. Imputed data count as missing.
evidence_needed: For yes or probably yes, actual outcome-availability evidence can be comparable observed-outcome counts, arm-specific loss-to-follow-up or censoring accounting, or an explicit complete/nearly-complete ascertainment statement.

Compare the approved outcome/time point across participant-flow and outcome-data passages. For each comparable arm or unit distinguish the randomized denominator, outcome-observed count, analysed count, imputed count, post-randomization excluded count, and event count. An event count is a numerator, not an outcome-observed count; an analysis denominator is not necessarily an outcome-observed count. Calculate randomized minus observed only when population, arm, unit, and time point are the same. Imputed data count as missing.

Keep outcome availability separate from mitigation quality: a sensitivity analysis or imputation does not change the observed count, and observed cannot be inferred as analysed minus imputed unless the source establishes the same population, time window, and mutually exclusive counts.
questions.no_information_rule: Answer no_information when the extent of missing outcome data remains unknown after bounded retrieval. Lack of evidence for complete availability is not evidence of materially incomplete availability.

answer_anchors.text: Outcome data were available for all or nearly all randomized participants.

considerations: The appropriate population is all randomized participants, not only participants included in a final analysis. Keep outcome availability distinct from exclusions for analysis or conduct; the same passage may inform both Domains for different scientific reasons.

Distinguish administrative censoring at a common data cutoff from censoring caused by missing follow-up; inspect actual rates and follow-up accounting rather than treating a generic censoring rule as outcome-availability evidence.

For time-to-event Results, treatment discontinuation or last-known-alive censoring does not by itself establish that outcome observation stopped; identify the actual observation endpoint, censoring reason, and follow-up pathway. For mortality, recovery or discharge does not establish vital status at a later time point. A total combining completed follow-up, recovery, and death does not establish mortality availability. If availability remains unresolved, inspect outcome-status or missing-value tables, including supplements. Match their outcome and time window to the approved Result. For dichotomous outcomes, compare unknown outcomes with observed events. Recovery may inform bias from missingness, but does not make unknown vital status observed.

Neutral paired control: complete ascertainment and an analysis denominator with unresolved ascertainment differ only in the availability premise; administrative censoring and worsening-related follow-up loss differ only in the missingness mechanism.

guidance: Answer every initially active question plus each dependent question whose activation predicate is met by your earlier answers. Extra inactive branch answers are ignored and never committed. Preserve the approved Result target.

Evaluate activated questions in question order. Submit every activated question with a justification, unknowns, and counterevidence. Review the inspected passages against its exact proposition and check material contradictions. Reuse adequate Evidence. When a premise remains unresolved, state the unresolved premise and why you stopped, and use bounded discovery across relevant Sources, including a protocol or SAP when relevant. Inspect returned passages before using them. A limitation requires that explicit premise and stopping rationale; include a Trial-scoped search receipt when retrieval provenance is useful, but a direct read does not require a search receipt. Absence requires a scoped untruncated no-hit receipt.

Cite complete premises for the active question. One passage may support several facts. When an answer depends on separate passages, cite each with its own boundaries. A relationship kind describes the use of Evidence; it adds no scientific fact.

When inference, conflict, or uncertainty connects Evidence to an answer, include a concise question-specific justification. State what the passages establish, what remains unresolved, and why the selected option follows. Any support relationship is host-asserted: the server checks structure, ownership, and exact Evidence provenance but does not independently judge semantic entailment.

Working premise records are source-grounded resumable notes. Reuse them only when the working checkpoint is current for this exact approved Result and captured Source projection; a stale checkpoint requires the stated recovery action and never carries a prior Domain judgment into this assessment.
A definitive yes or no needs direct_support, indirect_support, or contradiction; a limitation or absence alone supports uncertainty, not a definitive answer.

Evaluate activation against your draft answers. If validation reports missing active question IDs, add those questions with allowed answer values and supported bases, then resubmit the complete active set in one validation call. The server commits only active answers.

Apply every reported repair and retain other drafted answers. Add missing questions to the existing answer set. Resolve further activation from the repaired answers before resubmitting. The server ignores inactive answers.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.
response_framework.quotation_rule: Brief direct quotations from the text of the study report should be used whenever possible to support the answer.

traps: A no-hit search describes one lexical query, not scientific absence.
A planned method does not prove conduct; a time origin or analysis population does not prove complete follow-up or equal assessment.
An endpoint label or definition does not prove objectivity, blinding, prespecification, or no alternative analyses.
A treatment assignment or visibly different intervention does not by itself prove that participants or personnel knew the assignment.
Different treatment or visit schedules do not by themselves prove that outcome measurement differed between groups.
Stratification does not prove allocation concealment.

guidance: Answer every initially active question plus each dependent question whose activation predicate is met by your earlier answers. Extra inactive branch answers are ignored and never committed. Preserve the approved Result target.

Evaluate activated questions in question order. Submit every activated question with a justification, unknowns, and counterevidence. Review the inspected passages against its exact proposition and check material contradictions. Reuse adequate Evidence. When a premise remains unresolved, state the unresolved premise and why you stopped, and use bounded discovery across relevant Sources, including a protocol or SAP when relevant. Inspect returned passages before using them. A limitation requires that explicit premise and stopping rationale; include a Trial-scoped search receipt when retrieval provenance is useful, but a direct read does not require a search receipt. Absence requires a scoped untruncated no-hit receipt.

Cite complete premises for the active question. One passage may support several facts. When an answer depends on separate passages, cite each with its own boundaries. A relationship kind describes the use of Evidence; it adds no scientific fact.

When inference, conflict, or uncertainty connects Evidence to an answer, include a concise question-specific justification. State what the passages establish, what remains unresolved, and why the selected option follows. Any support relationship is host-asserted: the server checks structure, ownership, and exact Evidence provenance but does not independently judge semantic entailment.

Working premise records are source-grounded resumable notes. Reuse them only when the working checkpoint is current for this exact approved Result and captured Source projection; a stale checkpoint requires the stated recovery action and never carries a prior Domain judgment into this assessment.
A definitive yes or no needs direct_support, indirect_support, or contradiction; a limitation or absence alone supports uncertainty, not a definitive answer.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.
response_framework.quotation_rule: Brief direct quotations from the text of the study report should be used whenever possible to support the answer.

guidance: Answer every initially active question plus each dependent question whose activation predicate is met by your earlier answers. Extra inactive branch answers are ignored and never committed. Preserve the approved Result target.

Evaluate activated questions in question order. Submit every activated question with a justification, unknowns, and counterevidence. Review the inspected passages against its exact proposition and check material contradictions. Reuse adequate Evidence. When a premise remains unresolved, state the unresolved premise and why you stopped, and use bounded discovery across relevant Sources, including a protocol or SAP when relevant. Inspect returned passages before using them. A limitation requires that explicit premise and stopping rationale; include a Trial-scoped search receipt when retrieval provenance is useful, but a direct read does not require a search receipt. Absence requires a scoped untruncated no-hit receipt.

Cite complete premises for the active question. One passage may support several facts. When an answer depends on separate passages, cite each with its own boundaries. A relationship kind describes the use of Evidence; it adds no scientific fact.

When inference, conflict, or uncertainty connects Evidence to an answer, include a concise question-specific justification. State what the passages establish, what remains unresolved, and why the selected option follows. Any support relationship is host-asserted: the server checks structure, ownership, and exact Evidence provenance but does not independently judge semantic entailment.

Working premise records are source-grounded resumable notes. Reuse them only when the working checkpoint is current for this exact approved Result and captured Source projection; a stale checkpoint requires the stated recovery action and never carries a prior Domain judgment into this assessment.
A definitive yes or no needs direct_support, indirect_support, or contradiction; a limitation or absence alone supports uncertainty, not a definitive answer.

Evaluate activation against your draft answers. If validation reports missing active question IDs, add those questions with allowed answer values and supported bases, then resubmit the complete active set in one validation call. The server commits only active answers.

Apply every reported repair and retain other drafted answers. Add missing questions to the existing answer set. Resolve further activation from the repaired answers before resubmitting. The server ignores inactive answers.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.
response_framework.quotation_rule: Brief direct quotations from the text of the study report should be used whenever possible to support the answer.

traps: A no-hit search describes one lexical query, not scientific absence.
A planned method does not prove conduct; a time origin or analysis population does not prove complete follow-up or equal assessment.

A treatment assignment or visibly different intervention does not by itself prove that participants or personnel knew the assignment.
Different treatment or visit schedules do not by themselves prove that outcome measurement differed between groups.
Stratification does not prove allocation concealment.

questions.decision_rule: Compare the approved Result with the applicable plan for the exact intervention comparison, cohort, endpoint, time window, population, analysis, and effect measure. Distinguish source creation/version and amendment dates from trial events and retrieval time; only compare chronology when the relevant events and precision are established. Changes made before unblinded data were available, or clearly unrelated to results such as a broken machine, do not raise concerns.
evidence_needed: A sufficiently detailed protocol or SAP, its source-located chronology and finalization date relative to unblinded outcome data, and the reported analysis.

For an original plan and an amended plan, capture the source-located content and chronology separately. An embedded SAP can be applicable evidence when its comparison, cohort, and Result fields match; an absent or unresolved plan remains an information limit.
questions.no_information_rule: Use a definitive answer when firm evidence establishes timing and correspondence. Use a probable answer when source facts and trial circumstances support only an inference. Use no_information when neither is supported. A plan mention or matching endpoint alone does not establish timing.

considerations: Assess correspondence between the applicable plan and the exact approved Result: outcome, time point, population, effect measure, and analysis must be compared.

Assess applicability before chronology: a platform or master plan may cover several comparisons and cohorts, so its presence does not establish applicability to the approved Result. Establish chronology separately: plan finalization must precede availability of unblinded outcome data; a source creation date, registry posting or update date, amendment date, or retrieval date is not automatically the relevant trial chronology.

Current registry content does not establish unseen historical intent, and a data cutoff is not investigator unblinding. Preserve unresolved applicability or chronology instead of filling the gap from report wording that merely looks prespecified.

Results-driven selection is a separate concern from whether a plan exists or whether its chronology is known. Do not infer selection merely from an amendment or from a mismatch without evidence that the choice was driven by results.

Neutral paired control: an applicable plan for the approved cohort differs from a platform plan for another phase; pre-unblinding finalization differs from ambiguous chronology only in the timing premise.

response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.

We assigned men with metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to receive
either ADT plus docetaxel (at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of body-surface
area every 3 weeks for six cycles) or ADT alone. The primary objective was to test
the hypothesis that the median overall survival would be 33.3% longer among
patients receiving docetaxel added to ADT early during therapy than among pa-
tients receiving ADT alone.

1|Background
2|This study's statistical analysis plan was contained within the protocol document in the section entitled
3|"Statistical Considerations". This is Section 9 of the protocol and can be found on page 40 of the original
4|protocol. As described below, there were significant changes to the statistical analysis plan in Addendum
5|3, dated July 9, 2008, and in Addendum 5, dated December 7, 2011. The final version of the protocol
6|reflects the statistical analysis plan after that addendum.
7|The protocol describes the interim analysis plans for the study, which were timed to correspond to
8|semiannual meetings of the ECOG Data Monitoring Committee. Information for these analyses is
9|extracted from the clinical database exactly eight weeks prior to each meeting. Thus, the information
10|proportions would not align exactly with the hypothetical table provided in the protocol.
11|At the time data were extracted for the Data Monitoring Committee meeting of October 2013, there was
12|53% information for the efficacy analysis. Pre-specified criteria for significance were reached, and the
13|Data Monitoring Committee released the data for presentation. Once this decision was made, the study
14|had essentially achieved "full" information, so the data was finalized soon thereafter in terms of the
15|primary endpoint. This report thus represents data with a cutoff for survival of December 23, 2013. No
16|further updates were made in order to preserve the Type I error. Data cleaning continued for other
17|aspects of the study, including treatment, adverse events, and secondary endpoints. All other data in this
18|report apart from survival reflect the database as of December 23, 2014.
19|Original design
20|The primary endpoint of this study is overall survival. The study population consists of prostate cancer
21|patients with extensive metastatic disease (high volume disease). Patients were stratified based on age
22|(≥70 versus <70), performance status (0-1 versus 2), prior adjuvant hormonal therapy (>12 months versus
23|≤12 months), intended use of combined androgen blockade >30 days from start of treatment, and
24|bisphosphonate use (bisphosphonate was then changed to "FDA approved drugs for delaying skeletal
25|related events" in addendum 5).
26|Survival time was to be compared between the chemohormonal therapy arm (Arm A) and the androgen
27|ablation arm (Arm B) by the log-rank test. This study was designed to detect a 33.3% improvement in
28|median survival time from 24 months in the androgen ablation arm to 32 months in the chemohormonal
29|therapy arm, corresponding to a hazard ratio of 1.33, with one-sided Type I error of 0.025. Planned full
30|information was 408 deaths, which provided 80% power, allowing for the interim analysis schedule
31|described below.
32|Accrual of 12 eligible patients per month for 45 months (568 total patients allowing a 5% ineligibility
33|rate) followed by 36 months of follow-up was anticipated to achieve full information. Interim analyses
34|were to be performed for all semi-annual ECOG Data Monitoring Committee meetings beginning when
35|approximately 25% of the planned full information events had occurred, about 29 months after the study
36|opens, continuing every 6 months until either the criterion for early stopping was met or full information
37|was reached. The truncated O'Brien-Fleming group sequential boundary was used to adjust for the
38|sequential testing.

9|Statistical Considerations
10|9.1
11|Introduction
12|This is the second revision of the statistical considerations section. The first
13|changes reflect design changes incorporated in addendum 3. Addendum 3
14|expanded study eligibility to all patients with both low and high volume metastatic
15|disease; eligibility was no longer restricted to patients with high volume disease.
16|High volume disease is defined as visceral metastases and/or bone metastases
17|(at least 4 or more bone lesions, and one of which must be outside of the
18|vertebral column AND pelvis). The duration between beginning of prior hormonal
19|therapy and registration was also changed from 90 days to 120 days.
20|Furthermore, an additional stratification factor was added in this addendum,
21|extent of disease: high vs. low volume disease.
22|The second revision is to increase the number of patients to be accrued from 600
23|patients to 780 patients. This is based on data from S9346 demonstrating that
24|the overall survival of men with prostate cancer starting androgen deprivation
25|therapy (ADT) in the modern era is longer than the historical data which was
26|used to develop the assumptions of addendum 3. In addition, the estimated
27|proportion of patients with high volume disease is also changed based on the
28|preliminary data released from the ECOG-ACRIN Data Monitoring Committee
29|(DMC) meeting in September, 2011. As such, the projections which are guiding
30|the statistical design need to be updated and require a trial of 780 patients.
31|9.2
32|Endpoints
33|The primary clinical endpoint is the difference across treatments in overall
34|survival. Patients will be stratified based on age, ECOG PS, use of combined
35|androgen blockade and FDA approved drugs for delaying skeletal related events,
36|time of prior adjuvant hormonal therapy, and extent of disease; no subgroup
37|analyses are planned. Primary endpoint will be studied for all intent-to-treat
38|patients.
39|Secondary endpoints include PSA response, change of PSA over time, time to
40|hormone refractory disease, time to clinical progression and time to PSA
41|progression. All patients who receive treatment, regardless of eligibility, will be
42|evaluated for toxicity.
43|9.3
44|Sample Size and Accrual
45|Based on prior studies and the preliminary data from SWOG study S9346, there
46|will be approximately 50% of patients with high volume disease and 50% of
47|patients with low volume disease in this population. Median survivals in arm B
48|were expected to be 24 months and 48 months for patients with high and low
49|volume disease, respectively. Under these assumptions above, the study
50|required 600 patients to be accrued and randomized equally to each of the two
51|arms (300 patients per arm). With the projected accrual rate of 8 patients per
52|month, the accrual goal was to be reached in 75 months with a follow up period
53|of 2.5 years.
54|Data from S9346 in the modern era indicates that median overall survival of men
55|treated with ADT and having low volume disease is approximately 67 months.
56|Rev. 12/11
57|Rev. 6/14

2|E3805
3|Cancer Research Group
4|Version Date: December 23, 2014
5|
6|NCI Update Date: June 15, 2011
7|48
8|The median overall survival for men with high volume disease is 33 months. This
9|is probably due to active agents for castrate resistant prostate cancer and stage
10|migration. The study is designed to demonstrate a 25% reduction in the survival
11|hazard rate, which corresponds to an improvement in median overall survival
12|from 33 months to 44 months in patients with high volume disease and from 67
13|months to 89.3 months in patients with low volume disease. After the activation
14|of addendum 3, E3805 was enrolling approximately 12 patients per month and
15|exceeds the anticipated accrual rate of 8 patients per month detailed in
16|addendum 3. In addition, based on the preliminary data released from the DMC
17|meeting in September, 2011, about 70% of patients have high volume disease
18|on this study. With the assumptions above, the study will need 780 patients to
19|maintain adequate power, and the accrual will be completed in 5.5 years with
20|additional 1.5 years for follow-up.
21|9.4
22|Primary Objective
23|The study will have 80% power to detect a 33.3% improvement in median overall
24|survival across treatments, using a log-rank test stratified on age, ECOG PS, use
25|of combined androgen blockade and FDA approved drugs for delaying skeletal
26|related events, time of prior adjuvant hormonal therapy, and extent of disease
27|with a one-sided 0.025 significance level. The primary comparison will be an
28|intent-to-treat analysis including all randomized patients.
29|Interim analyses will be performed for all semi-annual ECOG-ACRIN DMC
30|meetings beginning when approximately 25% of the planned full information has
31|occurred, about 35.5 months, continuing every 6 months until either criterion for
32|early stopping are met or full information is reached. Twenty-five percent of the
33|full information under the alternative hypothesis is equal to 100 failures. Full
34|information will be achieved when 399 patients have died. The final analysis is
35|scheduled for this time point. This study will be monitored for early stopping in
36|favor of the null hypothesis using repeated confidence interval methodology
37|similar to that described by Jennison and Turnbull, 1990 (Statistical Science
38|5:299-317). At each interim analysis the nominal (1-2 X alpha) confidence
39|interval on the overall survival hazard ratio comparing arm B to arm A will be
40|computed, where alpha is the nominal one-sided significance level of the use
41|function boundary at the information fraction for the particular analysis time. If the
42|upper bound of the repeated confidence interval is smaller than 1.33, then the
43|data monitoring committee may consider closing an arm of the trial or stopping
44|the study early for overall lack of treatment differences. Under the accrual and
45|failure rate assumptions above, the following table gives the expected interim
46|analysis times, information times, and the corresponding truncated O'Brien
47|Fleming boundaries (K. Lan and D. DeMets, 1983, Biometrika 70(3):659-663).
48|Information from interim analyses will be reviewed by the DMC, who may decide
49|to stop the study early if efficacy or futility has been demonstrated. Because of
50|delays in initiation of accrual and delays in data submission and processing, it is
51|likely that the actual analysis times will be 6-12 months later.
